content:
deploy-bot: Deploy kicked off for release/voice-embed-v3 — canary 10% across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. tag: v3.2.1

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: embed-service 5xx-rate > 8% (canary slice) — autopage fired to #incidents and paging on-call. Rule: canary-5xx-threshold.

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PDINC12345 — triggered by embed-service-5xx (priority: P1).

ryan-oncall: ack PDINC12345 — I'm on it, switching to incident bridge. Investigating logs now.

luke-eng: on-call hunt? pinging runtime team. I can join in 2m. any customer reports yet?

anjali-pm: Customer 42 (voice analytics) reported elevated error rate at ~12:02 UTC via support ticket. Marking potential impact.

incident-bot: Canary traffic snapshot: 1000 req/min, error spike began at 12:01:14 UTC, p50 latency steady, p95 increased by ~180ms.

ryan-oncall: quick tail of logs from canary pod: `embed-service` shows repeated tokenizer errors then OOMs on quant path. snippet: ```
ERROR TokenizerFailure: invalid token length
GPU memory spike: 12.3GB -> 15.9GB
```

sara-runtime: that sounds like the new tokenizer changes in v3.2.1 — we added a fallback that allocates extra KV cache. I'm rolling up metrics for quantized workers.

luke-eng: if quant path is OOMing we should stop routing to quant variants and fallback to float32 for canary. Can we toggle routing policy?

ryan-oncall: agreeing. Plan: 1) Pause canary rollout traffic -> hold at 0% new user traffic, 2) Flip routing to prefer float path, 3) If errors persist rollback. Who can run the routing toggle?

sara-runtime: I can flip route policy. command in control plane: `redwoodctl route update embed-service --variant float --scope canary`

ryan-oncall: do it now and notify PD.

[sara-runtime] executed command: `redwoodctl route update embed-service --variant float --scope canary`

incident-bot: Route update applied. Canary traffic now served by float variant (approx 10% traffic). Observability: starting to sweep metrics for 1m.

pd-bot: PDINC12345 status: acknowledged by ryan-oncall. Escalation timer paused.

tess-support: drafting customer note: "We're seeing a canary-related regression affecting embeddings for some users; we've applied a mitigation and are monitoring. Will update in 30m." Should I send to affected customers now?

anjali-pm: yes send a short note to primary contacts. Mark SLA risk. Add that rollback is a possible follow-up.

incident-bot: Metrics 3m after route flip: 5xx rate down to 1.1% (from 8.3%), p95 latency back to baseline. No new OOMs observed.

ryan-oncall: good sign. however I'm seeing a small surge of 5xx on eu-west-1 edge — lower magnitude. keeping watch.

luke-eng: we should still consider rollback; the tokenizer change touched a shared library. Prefer full rollback to v3.2.0 until we validate new tokenizer. Who approves?

sara-runtime: I'll prep the rollback job. Command: ```
redwoodctl release rollback embed-service --to v3.2.0 --regions us-east-1,eu-west-1
```

ryan-oncall: rollbacks require lead approval for production. luke-eng can you approve?

luke-eng: approve rollback to v3.2.0 for canary + staged. go ahead. :white_check_mark:

[sara-runtime] kicked rollback job. Logs: ```
Rolling back embed-service -> v3.2.0
Stopping canary pods: OK
Deploying v3.2.0 to canary slice: OK
Verifying health checks: OK
```

incident-bot: Rollback complete. Telemetry: 5xx rate ~0.2%, p95 stable. PDINC12345: setting to resolved candidate pending post-deploy validation.

pd-bot: PDINC12345: incident resolved by ryan-oncall. Resolution notes: canary rollout caused tokenizer regression; mitigated by routing to float variant and rollback to v3.2.0.

ryan-oncall: marking incident resolved in PD. Leaving notes and runbook links. We should create a short postmortem and flag the tokenizer change for a gated rollout with canary traffic at lower % and chaos tests for quant path.

anjali-pm: I'll open a customer-facing follow-up with timeline and apology. Add remediation: longer validation and a docs blurb on model-path toggles.

luke-eng: action items: 1) revert tokenizer change patch and add unit tests (sara-runtime + eng team), 2) add canary healthchecks for quant memory growth, 3) update deployment runbook to include quick routing toggle steps and rollback checklist.

tess-support: customer messages sent. One customer replied: thanks for the fast mitigation, will wait for follow-up.

ryan-oncall: thanks all. I'll close the bridge after 20m of stable metrics. If anything pops we reopen.

incident-bot: Bridge closed by ryan-oncall at +18m after stable checks. Postmortem: to be filed in #postmortems with tag `canary-tokenizer-regress`.
